phrasings: What kind of research do you do?
intents.reply: I'm Researcher. I read interview notes, surveys and figures and summarise them in a page or less, saying where each point comes from and when evidence is thin. Ask me for a summary and I'll write it for you in your space.

phrasings: What's on your plate right now?
What are you doing at the moment?
intents.reply: In Customer research I'm summarising Alex's three client interviews (RES-2): one page per interview, then a page of what they have in common. After that comes comparing the findings with last year (RES-4). In Quarterly report, I collected this quarter's figures (QTR-1), which Writer is now using for the summary.

phrasings: How are the interview summaries going?
Are the interview notes summarised yet?
What's the status of the interview summaries?
intents.reply: The three interview summaries, RES-2, are written; the page of what they have in common is left. All three clients trust us on delivery dates.

phrasings: Summarise what clients say about keeping them informed
Write me a summary of the interviews

Get going on a summary for me
Research how we keep clients informed
intents.reply: I've started a task in your space: a one-page summary of what Alex's three client interviews say about keeping clients informed, with the source of each point and where the evidence is thin. Follow the run from the task; it comes back here when it ends.

input.title: Summarise what clients say about keeping them informed
input.description: From the three client interviews in Customer research: what clients say about dates, check-ins and being told when something slips. One page, the source of each point, and what the evidence does not cover.

phrasings: Where is customer research up to?
Give me an overview of the research
How is the research project going?
intents.reply: Customer research is Alex's project. The three client interviews are done (RES-1) and I'm finishing their summaries (RES-2). Priya has the survey questions to write (RES-3), I compare with last year after that (RES-4), and sharing the findings with the studio (RES-5) is in the backlog.

phrasings: What do clients say about delivery dates?
intents.reply: All three clients said they trust us on delivery dates. One wants a check-in halfway through a project; another wants early warning when a date slips.

phrasings: What does Knowledge say about our decisions?
Why is the site built as static pages?
intents.reply: Website relaunch's Knowledge holds two decisions. Building the site as static pages is accepted: it changes a few times a month, and static pages are cheaper to host with nothing to keep patched. Giving every case study the same four headings is still proposed, so it's worth a decision before WEB-4 is written.
